content.comment_body: Hello, I am using five [product_name] modules ([article_no]) for a home automation project. I use the network feature to share status between the devices. For example, a switch connected to module 1 sends its state to module 2 to control a light. My setup is: On module 1, an input (I1) with a latching relay connected to a flag M1. Ethernet is set up as a server connection. On module 2, there is a network input (NI1) mapped to an output (Q1), with Ethernet configured as a client of module 1. Data transfer is set to read 1 byte from VB10 (local) to MB0 (remote). Everything works well in simulation and mostly in reality, but sometimes there’s a delay of up to 10 seconds before the light changes state. Any ideas on the cause of this delay?
Hi, it may be helpful if you share your project code here for review.
Hello everyone, I have attached my project code. If anyone has suggestions or insights, please share. Thanks [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: A user reported noticeable latency—sometimes up to 10 seconds—while using multiple [product_name] modules ([article_no]) and Ethernet communication in a home automation setup. The overall system operates but can be slow to update input statuses between devices in real use, despite simulations showing prompt performance.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is seeking reliable and rapid Ethernet-based transfer of input signals between [product_name] modules, with real-world performance matching the near-instant response seen during simulation.
